plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial grown in gardens across the Northern Hemisphere, producing dense, layered blooms in many forms including pompon, spider, and incurved types. It tolerates light frosts and provides color when most other garden plants are fading.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: In Japan, the chrysanthemum is the emblem of the Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Festival is held in autumn to celebrate it.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in late autumn, earlier than its relative Camellia japonica. Its fragrant, delicate flowers with prominent yellow stamens attract late-season pollinators and brighten the landscape as temperatures cool.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Oil pressed from the seeds of Camellia sasanqua is used in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tree of the Southern Hemisphere spring that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the fern-like leaves fully emerge. Its fallen blossoms carpet streets and pavements in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A daisy-like annual with feathery foliage that blooms prolifically in warm climates. In frost-free regions of the Northern Hemisphere and in the spring gardens of the Southern Hemisphere, it keeps flowering through early November, attracting bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost; spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Mexico; naturalized in warm regions of the Americas, Australia, and Asia
plants.funFact: The name 'cosmos' comes from the Greek word for 'order' or 'harmony,' reflecting the symmetrical arrangement of its petals.
